assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hardware correction of the spherical aberration of electron lenses opened the door to routine sub-angstrom imaging and spectroscopy of atoms in interfaces, defects and nanostructures. It is a genuine invention with demonstrated, field-wide consequences for materials physics, chemistry and biology. I declare my own field's closeness and have tried to judge by the record rather than familiarity.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the multipole corrector design and theory, Haider led the first working implementation, and Urban led the demonstration of atomic-resolution gains with the corrected instrument. This is a natural three-person configuration. Zach, Scherzer's earlier ideas and the Krivanek (STEM) work are not in the supplied credit, and the historical record of who did what first should be checked carefully.
assessment.maturity: Corrected instruments have been commercial for about two decades and are confirmed independently by many laboratories. Recognition is well timed; it has been a long-standing omission.
uncertainties: Whether prior recognition of the same people (e.g. the Wolf Prize) and the omission of Krivanek from the supplied credit raise attribution questions.
Whether the committee regards a microscopy instrument invention as sufficiently fundamental physics, and whether my professional proximity requires extra caution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of the Higgs boson in 2012 by two independent experiments completed the Standard Model's electroweak sector and verified an experiment-defining prediction. It is among the most clearly verified discoveries in modern physics, and the 2013 prize recognised the theory but not the experimental discovery.
assessment.attribution: The collaborations count thousands of members, so a fair prize is difficult. Jenni and Della Negra founded and led ATLAS and CMS respectively, and Virdee was a founding figure and spokesperson of CMS. Gianotti led ATLAS at the time of announcement and is a strong alternative; I cannot resolve this fairly from the supplied credit and would want the historical record of the conception and leadership examined.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature: confirmed by two independent experiments, with properties measured over a decade at the LHC. Timing is ripe, with the original-experiment criterion satisfied.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among collaboration leaders versus the many who built detectors and analyses; statutes limit the prize to three people.
Whether to prefer founding leadership over leadership at the time of discovery; I have not independently verified the details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, based on trapping neutral atoms at the magic wavelength, has delivered fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and underpins a redefinition of the second, tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and searches for new physics. It is a clear invention that opened a door to measurements previously out of reach.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and carried out the first demonstrations; Ye drove the performance to the current record and the broader program with Hall-style frequency combs. Two proposed laureates is a clean configuration, though Hall-related comb work was already prized in 2005 and the contribution of other groups (e.g. Lemonde, Takamoto) should be considered.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation across many national metrology institutes. Timing is arguably good, though the redefinition of the second is still pending, which might make a later date reasonable.
uncertainties: Whether the ion-clock and Al+ clock communities merit joint recognition.
Extent to which the primary benefit is yet to be realised in practice.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2008 discovery of superconductivity in fluorine-doped LaFeAsO opened a second family of high-temperature superconductors and a large experimental field. It is an original experimental discovery with clear lasting impact on the understanding of unconventional pairing.
assessment.attribution: Hosono is the single credited name and the discovery paper is clearly from his group, so attribution is unusually clean. Coworkers in the original paper (e.g. Kamihara) are not in the supplied credit and could be examined.
assessment.maturity: Well replicated worldwide within months and developed over 15+ years; the mechanism of pairing remains debated, but the discovery itself is secure. Timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Mechanism remains unsettled, though a prize for discovery does not require it.
Whether a single-laureate prize is the best representation of the original work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos by IceCube in 2013 and the later identification of a flaring blazar and the Galactic plane opened neutrino astronomy as a new window on the high-energy universe. It is a clear observational discovery from a new kind of instrument.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube and Karle was a central figure in its construction and operation. The credit omits other founders and the earlier AMANDA contributors, and the collaboration is large; this needs historical examination.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed through multiple analyses and source associations (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068, Galactic plane), but source populations are still not well understood. Timeliness is plausible rather than pressing.
uncertainties: Few firmly identified sources so far; the full astrophysical interpretation is incomplete.
Credit shared with the wider IceCube and AMANDA community.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 1995 observation of large room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions was the original experiment that led to MRAM and modern read heads. It is a classic invention with major practical impact following the 2007 prize for giant magnetoresistance.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera independently reported room-temperature TMR in 1995 and are the original experimenters. Parkin's later work on MgO-based junctions is a distinct, later improvement, which is why I would not include him on the original-experiment criterion, though this is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Over three decades of independent replication and industrial use. Timing is late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the later giant MgO TMR (Parkin; Yuasa; not in the credit) deserves equal weight.
Overlap with the 2007 GMR prize may weigh against.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect, its experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells, and the observation of the quantum anomalous Hall effect in magnetic topological insulators together form a coherent, verified discovery line of lasting importance to condensed matter physics and potential low-dissipation electronics.
assessment.attribution: Kane (theory), Molenkamp (experimental QSH) and Xue (QAH observation) cover distinct decisive steps. Mele, Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and others who proposed the HgTe route are absent from this credit, and the allocation among theory and experiment is contentious.
assessment.maturity: Both effects are confirmed by independent groups, though the QAH temperature scale remains very low and applications are not yet realised. Recognition is plausible but possibly early.
uncertainties: Dispute over who contributed the decisive theory (Kane-Mele versus Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang), which this credit does not resolve.
Practical impact is still limited by low operating temperatures.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 1992 detection of the first trans-Neptunian object beyond Pluto confirmed the Kuiper Belt and reshaped understanding of Solar System formation and migration. It is an original observation with large conceptual consequences, and one woman among the two credited discoverers.
assessment.attribution: Jewitt and Luu carried out the discovery observations and are a clean two-person credit. Theoretical predictions by Edgeworth and Kuiper, and others' contributions, are historical context not covered by the credit.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed by thousands of subsequent detections. Long established, so timing is not premature.
uncertainties: Whether Solar System astronomy sits within the physics prize remit as defined by the committee.
Allocation of credit relative to earlier theoretical suggestions.
